<!-- dozu-tracking:start -->
## Work tracking
Use the live **status:**, **priority:** and **complexity:** labels above; **Assignees** identifies the owner. These labels are separate from the task/ticket type.

**Planning complexity:** XL - Multi-OS packaging experiment with Node, PostgreSQL/pgvector and Python compatibility unknowns; split the proof into platform work.
Complexity is a provisional scope/uncertainty estimate, not a delivery-time commitment. XL work must be split into executable subtasks before starting.
**Planning priority:** P0 - Architecture/foundation work that unblocks the implementation path.
<!-- dozu-tracking:end -->

## Outcome
Recommend Electron with the existing Next.js standalone server, Express and local data/services. Validate packaged behavior instead of creating a second React/Vite UI.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Run a native packaged proof on Windows/macOS/Linux with full Next server semantics, local Express, PostgreSQL/pgvector and FastAPI/model.
- [ ] Verify Electron utilityProcess compatibility or bundle a pinned standalone Node runtime; no system Node/Python/database/Docker/WSL requirement.
- [ ] Exercise dynamic routes, locales/server messages, local data writes, files, sockets/streams, PDF/editor/media and a system-browser provider flow.
- [ ] Measure bundle size, RAM/startup, supported CPU/OS and native ABI/dynamic library compatibility; record evidence and resource budgets.
- [ ] Record architecture ADR; the proof is an early gate, not permission to reduce the first-release feature scope.

## Architecture constraints
The complete existing Next.js UI and Express backend run locally with a local database/files. Desktop and local browser use the same localhost backend. Real third-party integrations may use the internet; preserve them wherever feasible. No central Dozu backend, cloud database, synchronization, shared publisher secrets in installers, or simulated replacements. All pages/features remain in release scope.

<!-- dozu-roadmap:DECISION-STACK -->

Phase: 0 Requirements | Priority: P0

Parent roadmap: https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/issues/1

## Dependencies
- #3 - [Task] Audit complete UI/backend and local-first integration baselines
- #2 - [Ticket] Record local-first requirements and full feature-preservation matrix


<!-- dozu-proof-checklist:start -->
## Executable architecture proof (started 2026-11-10)

Shared component experiments execute in order; native platforms have explicit subissues. Evidence lives in local `planning/architecture-proof/` with sanitized logs/manifests/scripts. These unchecked gates do not change the acceptance criteria above.

- [ ] P1 — Measure pinned runtime/model/browser/font/conversion/transcription assets, hashes, complete footprint and installer feasibility; count every asset, report missing assets, no first-run downloads.
- [ ] P2 — Sanitized production build and Electron utilityProcess or pinned bundled Node startup of retained Next standalone + Express; dynamic en/vi routes, streams/sockets and process cleanup; fix only measured necessary build/runtime blockers.
- [ ] P3 — Disposable native PostgreSQL/pgvector: 20 migration hashes, extension, seeds, vector/cosine/HNSW/SQL contracts, local writes and restart persistence.
- [ ] P4 — Pinned offline CPU Python/model with fresh user paths, API consumer contract including known batch 500, startup/steady/processing memory and model/cache manifest.
- [ ] P5 — Native DOC/DOCX/TXT→PDF, URL→PDF/browser assets, whisper.cpp tiny + FFmpeg, fonts/licenses/libraries and real fixtures; no capability removed.
- [ ] P6 — Native packaged matrix on every approved OS/CPU baseline, clean installation without developer dependencies (subissues below). Cross-builds are not evidence.
- [ ] P7 — Complete-process cold/warm UI/backend timing, normal/peak RAM+CPU/size; loopback/auth/secret review, restart/upgrade/backup/uninstall keep/delete evidence and conditional ADR/options. Approved budgets stay unchanged.

### Native execution subissues
- [ ] #45 — windows: https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/issues/45
- [ ] #46 — macos: https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/issues/46
- [ ] #47 — linux: https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/issues/47

Current workspace is Windows only; macOS/Linux native acceptance remains unpassed. Shared experiments can progress here. No assignee is invented. P1–P5 are component checks; P6/P7 must still validate full packaged behavior on supported hardware.
<!-- dozu-proof-checklist:end -->

comments.body:
Baseline audit #3 is complete. The source-supported Electron/Next standalone + Express + PostgreSQL/pgvector + CPU FastAPI recommendation remains conditional on this proof.

Please include actual additional processing dependencies: Gotenberg/LibreOffice DOC/DOCX/TXT→PDF, Puppeteer URL→PDF/browser assets, whisper.cpp tiny speech model and FFmpeg. No user Docker/WSL/runtime setup can be inherited. Source evidence is in local `planning/audit/systems.md`, `findings.md` and the full page matrix.

Known proof constraints: retained website build currently fails YoutubePlayerAdapter Promise<number>/number type validation; all 20 local migrations are Git-ignored; pgvector extension/first-boot seeds are not established; eager PayOS/mail/Redis initialization prevents a clean optional-provider startup profile. Real CPU 384-dimensional embedding works with the cached model, but batch `/segments/embedding` has an existing response-schema HTTP 500.

This handoff does not start or complete #4, reduce full feature scope, decide #41/#43 or establish all-platform packaging. See #3 completion evidence for commands, source commits and limitations.

User-approved Task #2 contract is now recorded in #2: Windows 10 22H2 legacy/Windows 11 primary x86-64, macOS 13+ Intel/ARM64, Ubuntu 22.04/Debian 12 x86-64; NSIS exe/dmg/deb (MSI optional, AppImage where compatible). Minimum 4 GB RAM/2 GB free/dual-core; low-resource mode required. Targets: 250 MB installer, 750 MB installed; minimum cold UI 10s/warm 5s/backend 8s/normal app memory 700 MB; recommended 5s/3s/4s/1 GB. Account for all runtimes/models/assets/processes. Benchmark in production on agreed minimum configurations; report evidence and an explicit recommendation before changing targets. SQLite is evaluation-only pending backend/vector/SQL/migration compatibility proof. LAN classrooms selected; payment execution explicitly deferred under #41. Read #2 for the full hardware/display/data lifecycle contract. This is a requirements handoff, not benchmark/packaging evidence.

First #4 proof work is recorded in local `planning/architecture-proof/report.md`, `results.json`, hashed input/resource manifests, sanitized logs and proposed `adr-0001.md`. No source/history import or source-tree edits; original UI/API/embedding repositories remain clean. These local evidence files have not been published as release artifacts.

Decomposition is linked in the issue body (P1–P7) and native subissues #45 Windows, #46 macOS, #47 Linux. They await shared component evidence, not parent closure. #4 remains `status:in-progress` / Project **In Progress**; no assignee inferred. Native subissues are waiting / Todo. Existing board columns and unrelated fields/items are preserved.

**Measured installed-size failure for the exact current Windows candidate:** model weight 470,641,600 bytes + actually loaded torch_cpu.dll 262,656,512 + executed Electron executable 249,831,936 = **983,130,048 bytes (983.130 MB)**. These three files alone exceed the approved **750 MB installed** target, before all other assets. Full snapshot is 479.729 MB; model-only XZ/LZMA2 preset-6 stream is **410.574 MB** versus 250 MB installer target. Compression is not an NSIS measurement or universal compressor bound. No budget was relaxed and no required resource was hidden in a first-run download.

**Verified narrowly on current Windows 11 x64 / i5-13400F / ~32 GB host:**
- Express production TypeScript compiles. Electron 45.2.3 (official SHA-verified Windows archive; bundled Node 24.22.2) executes actual compiled entrypoint, which fails readiness on eager mail URL requirements, then PayOS configuration after local URLs alone are supplied. Redis initialization and circular DB logger failure are recorded. No provider keys/fake provider success used.
- Unchanged Next build reproduces audited YouTube Promise/number failure. A disposable-copy runtime type-guard patch passes focused adapter checks and full production build/type validation; original website source is unchanged. Next's generated pages are retained.
- After resolving localhost binding/origin and a developer-dependency link in standalone output, a staged Next/React production closure serves en/vi welcome, a dynamic topic URL, vi login and a static JS chunk under Electron utilityProcess, with module resolution outside standalone rejected. Existing welcome UI renders in a hidden sandboxed window. **HTTP 200 is not parity**: topic SSR logs `location is not defined`, image optimization lacks `sharp`, and CSP warning remains. No auth/data/provider workflow passed.
- Real CPU FastAPI/model works with offline flags, fresh HF_HOME and explicit existing snapshot revision `86741b4e3f5cb7765a600d3a3d55a0f6a6cb443d`: single embedding 384 finite normalized values; identical comparison succeeds; existing batch **500** reproduced. Serial warm-cache readiness **6.332s**; worker WS after requests **762.409 MB**, private bytes **1,209.598 MB**. Existing venv includes optional spaCy/thinc, so this is not a minimal clean runtime benchmark. Native loaded DLLs are recorded. Earlier 45.369s run was contended and is not a cold benchmark.
- Electron+Next sampled group has five app-owned processes and **550.871 MB** last WS snapshot. API/DB/Python/converters were not in that group. No independent snapshots are presented as a concurrent full-app measurement; timing probes are not launch-to-interactive acceptance measurements.

**Unpassed/pending:** official native PostgreSQL binary and alternate EDB endpoint return HTTP 403 here; no cluster, pgvector, migrations/seeds, SQL writes or persistence tests executed. Portable Python/model installation, all document/URL/whisper.cpp/tiny/FFmpeg/font assets, complete NSIS/DMG/deb/AppImage, every supported native OS/CPU/minimum device, full interactive/cold/warm/normal-workload measurements, provider flow, security and upgrade/backup/uninstall remain open. No native Mac/Linux host is attached. The optional spaCy `en_core_web_sm` model is absent; its fallback/resource policy is now explicit in the proof report. Payments remain deferred/blocked under #41; classrooms remain LAN/user-owned host.

**Recommendation:** retain complete Next/Express while evaluating a smaller CPU embedding backend/quantized representation of the same multilingual model with en/vi numerical/retrieval/quality tests, and quantify native conversion/transcription resources. Browser reuse is only a proposed experiment. Keep PostgreSQL until compatibility evidence says otherwise. Proposed ADR is **not accepted**; **all #4 acceptance criteria/P1–P7 completion gates remain unchecked**, and no issue is closed by these experiments.
